A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DWIM paper and complete supplementary Sections 6–14. All 17 pages were compared using text extraction and rendered images; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv margin stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, generalization experiments and ablations in Section 4, plus human evaluations of action flagging and tool awareness in supplementary Sections 9–10.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations and supplementary human evaluations. Retained results qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The discrepancy-aware workflow generation, dynamic agentic framework, action flagging and instruct-masking procedure are identical, including Algorithm 1 and the supplementary method descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GQA, OKVQA, SugarCREPE, NaturalBench, RefCOCO and TallyQA, with A-OKVQA and Winoground additionally used for generalization. Task coverage and tool-library scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Frozen few-shot, VisRep, HYDRA and the same end-to-end reference models. The SFT and masking variants used as ablation comparators also remain identical.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical splits, accuracy and IoU metrics, backbone configurations, shot counts, training settings and inference procedures. Supplementary human-evaluation sample sizes and procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same prompting and tool-library analyses, workflow-generation and masking ablations, backbone experiments, qualitative examples, human assessments and failure cases in Figure 4, Tables 4–7 and supplementary Sections 7–12.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 reports averages over three runs with standard deviations in both versions. Run-count information and uncertainty-reporting practices are identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative outcomes match, including the appendices. For example, Table 2 retains DWIM's GQA score of 69.3 ± 1.0 and SugarCREPE score of 74.6 ± 1.3.

T1.justification: The task formulation, workflow-generation equations and training objectives in Equations 1–10 are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about discrepancy-aware generation, instruct-masking, improved tool awareness, state-of-the-art performance and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of efficiency, tool awareness and generalization are unchanged. Supplementary Sections 9 and 12 retain the same limitations concerning rule-based misflagging, incorrect workflows and tool failures.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, tool specifications, computational costs, prompt templates and interface code are identical across Section 4 and the supplementary material. Both provide the same code-repository link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, comparison positioning in Table 1 and all 69 reference entries are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from v1 dated 25 Mar 2025 to v2 dated 26 Jun 2025. Title, authors, prose, terminology, headings and document organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned and its gray tone changes marginally. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–9, Algorithm 1 and all remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, results, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations are identical throughout the main paper and appendices. Updating and slightly repositioning the arXiv stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
